title: Fluorescent in situ mRNA detection in the adult mouse cochlea
protocol: Euthanize four-week-old mice (postnatal day 28).
Decapitate the mouse.
Bisect the skull with two scissor cuts: one from the base of the brainstem above the skull to the nose, and another from the base of the brainstem to the lower jaw.
Remove the brain tissue to expose the otic capsules.
Dissect the otic capsule.
Create a window in the apex of the cochlea at the apical turn crease.
Extract each otic capsule by applying pressure with a gloved thumbnail above the apex of the cochlea.

Hold a bisected skull in the left hand and apply pressure to the tissue behind the otic capsule so that the capsule is pushed upwards, while simultaneously pushing down on the semicircular canal with the other thumb.
Remove the lifted otic capsule using RNase-free forceps.
Place the extracted otic capsule directly into 4% PFA solution.
Perfuse 4% PFA solution into the round and oval windows of the isolated otic capsule.
Transfer the isolated otic capsules into 4% PFA solution in a 35×10 mm dish coated with black Sylgard.
Place the curved sharp tip of a curved pair of sharp forceps or an 18-gauge needle along the crease of the apical cochlear turn and apply gentle pressure to remove a fragment of the apical bone.
Generate a small window at the apex.
Using a 30-gauge needle, slowly perfuse about 100 μL of 4% PFA solution into the round and oval windows.
Push the solution through the cochlea using gentle pressure at a flow rate of approximately 50 μL per minute.
Remove the stapes with forceps to allow for easier perfusion.
Incubate the perfused cochleae in a 2 mL Eppendorf tube containing 1.8 mL of 4% PFA solution.
Set the incubation conditions to gentle rocking at 4°C for 12–16 hours.
Separate the left and right cochleae into different Eppendorf tubes.
Transfer the cochleae into RNase-free 0.5 M EDTA solution pH 8.0 after overnight fixation.
Incubate the cochleae in EDTA for 3 hours with slow agitation at room temperature.
Rinse the cochleae once in RNase-free PBS.
Transfer the cochleae into RNase-free PBS at room temperature for dissection.
Insert one blade of Vannas Spring Scissors into the oval window and cut along the turn towards the apex after decalcification.
Place one scissor blade into the region cut in step 9 with the other on the back of the cochlea to separate the basal turn from the middle and apical turn.
Hold the apical/middle turn so that the apical end points down and cut along the scala media.
Place one scissor blade into the region cut in step 11 and place the other on the outside of the bony labyrinth to separate the middle and apical turns.
Cut the spiral ganglion fibers connecting to the basal turn and remove excess bone and tissue using scissors.
Transfer cochleae into RNase-free PBS without Ca2+/Mg2+ for dissection.
Use a sharp tip of a curved 18-gauge needle to chip away bone from the cochlear apical turn.
Gently hook the bone with the curved tip of the needle and chip it away from the apical window opening.
Continue chipping until all bone surrounding the sensory epithelium is removed.
Scrape the region between the stria vascularis and the bone with a sharp needle to gently separate the two compartments.
Bend the tip of the 18-gauge needle carefully to generate a sharp curved “hook”.
Dissect the apical turn using Vannas Spring Scissors.
Remove excess stria vascularis tissue with the scissors.
Transfer the apical turns to a 35×10 mm plastic Petri dish filled with RNase-Free PBS.
Use a 0.1 mm thick scalpel blade mounted to a blade holder to remove excess tissue.
After removing excess tissue, visualize the remaining hair cells in the apical turn.
Use a micro spoon to transfer fully immersed tissue.
Cut in half a sheet of Secure-Seal™ hybridization chamber system for two stripes of four chambers each.
Cut a piece of Post-it paper to the dimensions of a microscope slide and mark four ≈ 9 mm circles aligning with the circular hybridization chambers.
Place the marked Post-it paper on a microscope slide, aligning the sticky section with the frosted end of the slide.
Mount a Superfrost Plus microscope slide onto the visual guide using the sticky part of the Post-it paper to hold it in place.
Place 10 μL of RNAse-free PBS without Ca2+/Mg2+ onto the front of the Superfrost Plus microscope slide.
Transfer the sensory epithelium turns into the 10 μL PBS drop using a micro spoon and orient the turns using forceps under a dissection microscope.
Orient the tissue so that the hair cells are facing upwards with the bundles pointing toward the surface.
Carefully remove excess PBS with a pipette after the tissue specimens are correctly oriented.
Allow the samples to air dry for about 5 minutes.
Attach the hybridization chambers over the designated regions.
Fill the wells carefully with 50 μL RNase-free PBS.
Gently remove PBS from each well in the hybridization chamber.
Add 50 μL of diluted Proteinase K solution to each chamber.
Incubate for 2.5 min at room temperature.
Gently remove the Proteinase K solution using a pipette.
Perform three 30 s washes with 50 μL PBST followed by one 5 min wash with 50 μL PBST.
Pre-warm a humidified plastic chamber to 37°C.
Replace the PBS in each hybridization chamber with 50 μL of HCR probe hybridization buffer for pre-hybridization.
Pre-heat probe hybridization buffer to 37°C.
Pre-hybridize for 10 min inside the humidified chamber at 37°C.
Prepare probe hybridization solution by adding 2 μL of 1 μM probe stock to 250 μL of hybridization buffer.
Remove the pre-hybridization solution with a P200 pipette.
Add 50 μL of the probe hybridization solution into each of the hybridization chambers.
Place sealing tabs over the chamber port holes and press them tightly onto the holes.
Incubate overnight (12–16 h) at 37°C in the humidified chamber.
Remove the probe hybridization solution from the hybridization chambers.
Replace with HCR probe wash buffer pre-heated to 37°C using different pipette tips.
Incubate sample hybridization chambers at 37°C in 50 μL of 75% probe wash buffer / 25% 5× SSCT for 15 min.
Incubate sample hybridization chambers at 37°C in 50 μL of 50% probe wash buffer / 50% 5× SSCT for 15 min.
Incubate sample hybridization chambers at 37°C in 50 μL of 25% probe wash buffer / 75% 5× SSCT for 15 min.
Incubate sample hybridization chambers at 37°C in 50 μL of 100% 5× SSCT for 15 min.
Incubate samples in 5× SSCT for 5 min at room temperature.
Add 50 μL of amplification buffer into each hybridization chamber.
Incubate in a humidified chamber for 30 min at room temperature.
Equilibrate an aliquot of HCR amplification buffer to room temperature before use.
Aliquot 1 μL of hairpin H1 (3 μM stock) into a fresh tube for each hybridization chamber.
Aliquot 1 μL of hairpin H2 (3 μM stock) into a fresh tube for each hybridization chamber.
Heat the tubes containing hairpins at 95°C for 90 s and then snap-cool on ice in the dark for 5 min.
Prepare hairpin solution by adding snap-cooled H1 hairpins and snap-cooled H2 hairpins to amplification buffer at room temperature. Add 1 μL of each hairpin per 50 μL.
Remove the amplification buffer from the hybridization chambers.
Add 50 μL of the hairpin solution in amplification buffer into each of the hybridization chambers.
Seal the hybridization chambers with adhesive seal tabs and incubate overnight (12–16 h) in a dark humidified chamber at room temperature.
Remove excess hairpins by incubating slide hybridization chamber in 5× SSCT at room temperature twice for 30 min, followed by a single wash for 15 min.
Incubate with DAPI at 1:1000 in PBST for 15 min at room temperature.
Wash with PBST for 15 min at room temperature.
Replace PBST with 50 μL of 50% glycerol for each hybridization chamber.
Remove glycerol solution.
Remove the adhesive Secure-Seal™ hybridization system.
Add a drop of FluorSave™ Reagent onto each sample.
Place cover slip gently to avoid bubble formation.
Allow mounting solution to dry in the dark at room temperature for 1 h.
Add a small amount of clear nail polish along edge of the coverslip to secure it permanently.
Proceed with confocal microscopy image acquisition and analysis.
Equilibrate the sample for 5 min in antibody wash buffer after excess hairpins are removed.
Replace antibody wash buffer with blocking buffer and incubate at room temperature for 2 h.
Centrifuge primary antibody tube briefly prior to taking an aliquot.
Dilute primary antibody in antibody incubation buffer.
Dilute primary antibody as needed.
Add 50 μL of diluted primary antibody to each hybridization chamber.
Incubate the chambers overnight (12-16 h) at 4°C in a humidified box.
Wash three times with 50 μL of antibody wash buffer for 15 min each at room temperature.
Centrifuge the tube of secondary antibody briefly to collect all solution at the bottom of the tube.
Dilute secondary antibody as needed.
Add 50 μL of diluted secondary antibody solution to each hybridization chamber.
Incubate the chambers at room temperature for 60 min.
Wash three times with 50 μL of antibody wash buffer for 15 min each at room temperature.
Add 50 μL of DAPI solution (1:1000 DAPI dilution in PBST) to each chamber.
Incubate the chambers for 15 min at room temperature.
Replace DAPI solution with 50 μL of PBST.
Incubate for 15 min.
Remove PBST and add 50 μL of 50% glycerol to each hybridization chamber.
Remove glycerol solution and adhesive Secure-Seal™ hybridization system.
Add a drop of FluorSave™ Reagent onto each sample.
Place cover slip and allow to dry in the dark for 1 h at room temperature.
Add a small amount of clear nail polish along edge of the coverslip to permanently secure the coverslip.
